reasoning.step1:
1) Document classification
- Multiple invoice indicators present: title "RECHNUNG", "RECHNUNGSDATUM", "GESAMT", "MwSt", invoice number T3281701, line-item style cost block. No exclusion terms like "Mahnung" or "Zahlungserinnerung" dominate. => classify as invoice.

2) Locate invoice date
- "RECHNUNGSDATUM 29-Mrz-23" on page 1 and repeated on page 2. Extract exact string: "29-Mrz-23".

3) Locate Grand Total
- On page 2: "GESAMT EUR 780,05". Total clearly shown as 780,05. No conflicting totals. Extract amount as in source: 780,05.

4) Locate VAT rate, net amount, VAT amount
- Page 2 summary shows:
  - "ISCHENSUMME 655,50" (typo for "Zwischensumme"/"Zwischensumme" or "Zwischensumme" but context shows amount before VAT)
  - "MwSt 124,55"
  - Under table: lines "655,50 124,55 19%" repeated.
- Therefore Net = 655,50; Vat.Amount = 124,55; Vat.Rate = 19 (per rule remove % sign).

5) Sender VAT ID decision
- Two VAT IDs appear: "KUNDEN-UST.-ID-NR. DE815512007" (customer VAT) in header, and footer shows "VAT/USt.-Id.-Nr. DE812975416" for DHL Global Forwarding (sender block).
- Schema field "Sender.VatId" requests tax ID of the sender. The sender of the invoice appears to be DHL Global Forwarding (footer company block) with VAT DE812975416. Extract Sender.VatId = "DE812975416".
- Note: do not fill customer VAT into Sender.VatId because that would conflict with label.

6) Verify no inference / multiple occurrences
- All extracted values are explicitly present in the text; no guesses made.
- Only one VAT group is present; treat Vat.Rate, Net.Amount, Vat.Amount as that single group.

7) Preserve formatting/decimals
- Keep decimal places as in source (two decimals, comma as decimal separator in source). Final numeric representation will retain same decimal precision per rules.
